column2: Why should an altered community found in disease not be called a cause on that basis alone?
column3: Dysbiosis has no universal taxonomic definition, and illness, diet, drugs, transit and inflammation all change microbiota, so the change may be consequence rather than cause.

column2: What does a stool sample fail to represent, despite being the usual specimen?
column3: Stool is shed luminal material and does not directly represent mucosa, small intestine, proximal colon or biofilm, and it varies with collection, storage, oxygen, extraction and transit.

column2: How can a taxon appear to increase when its absolute count has not changed?
column3: Sequencing reports relative abundance, so the decline of another taxon raises the proportion occupied by an unchanged population.

column3: Shotgun sequencing resolves more genes and strains than marker-region amplification, but neither proves gene expression and shotgun also detects dead organisms.

column2: Why does culture remain valuable alongside sequencing?

column2: How do antibiotics change bile-acid biology in a way that favours Clostridioides difficile?
column3: They reduce microbial deconjugation and conversion to secondary bile acids, and the altered bile-acid environment changes germination and growth of Clostridioides difficile.

column2: Why is the association between trimethylamine N-oxide and cardiovascular outcomes hard to read causally?
column3: Diet supplies the choline and carnitine precursors and kidney clearance determines the concentration, so both confound the association and therapeutic causality is still under study.

column2: Why are facultative organisms that expand during inflammation best seen as markers and amplifiers?
column3: Inflammation raises oxygen and alternative electron acceptors and releases nutrients, so these organisms exploit conditions the host created, then worsen barrier and inflammation through feedback.

column3: Detection of a toxigenic organism without compatible diarrhoea may represent colonisation rather than infection, so testing patients without the syndrome mislabels carriers.

column2: Why does a randomised dietary or antibiotic intervention still leave attribution to the microbiota uncertain?
column3: These interventions have direct host effects as well as microbial ones, so an improved outcome need not have travelled through the proposed microbial mediator.

column2: Why are Koch's postulates difficult to apply to polymicrobial ecological disease?
column3: No single organism may be necessary or sufficient, so causal reasoning shifts to temporality, dose, manipulation, mechanism and reversibility, and a community function can be causal across differing taxonomic configurations.
